evals.prompt: Design and build a responsive booking site from this idea. We have no brief or visual references yet.
evals.expected_output: The common router begins with discovery, preserves the build objective as a later gated series, and stops at UX-brief approval.
expectations: product-design is the entrypoint and product-design-discovery is the first worker.
The likely route records direction, contract, prototype, implementation, review, and accept-freeze without launching past Gate A.
The first human gate is Gate A.

evals.prompt: Create a native iOS medication app from scratch, including the UX, visual design, and production screens.
evals.expected_output: The common router detects a new native Apple product, begins with discovery, preflights claim-relevant safety and platform capabilities, and does not jump to SwiftUI implementation.
expectations: product-design-discovery is the first worker.
The later route uses Apple-specific prototype, implementation, runtime, and accessibility adapters only after the prerequisite gates.
The first human gate is Gate A; a missing blocking capability may stop earlier for setup.

evals.prompt: Our UX brief is approved. Create and compare three visual directions for phone and desktop.
evals.expected_output: The router verifies the accepted brief and sends the request to direction rather than letting the worker bypass common preflight and state handling.
expectations: product-design-direction is the first worker.
The directions use matched content, states, targets, and render evidence.
The route stops at Gate B for human selection.

evals.prompt: The product structure and visual direction are approved. Make a clickable account-recovery mock before we touch production.
evals.expected_output: The router selects an isolated prototype after confirming the accepted inputs and keeps production and baselines protected.
expectations: product-design-prototype is the first worker when the contract or equivalent accepted input is sufficient.
The prototype remains isolated and disposable.
A representative slice stops at Gate C before production implementation.

evals.prompt: Convert this named approved Figma mock, including its loading, error, long-content, phone, and desktop states, into reusable Vue components.
evals.expected_output: The router sends a sufficiently explicit approved reference to implementation and protects accepted baselines.
expectations: product-design-implementation is the first worker when the immutable reference maps unambiguously to the existing component system.
The implementation envelope records bounded-reviewed-slice and its durable human approval ID.
The route becomes contract first if state, adaptation, identity, or source mapping is insufficient.
Implementation is followed by read-only review and Gate D candidate disposition; Gate E approval and accept-freeze remain separate.

evals.prompt: Tighten the accepted checkout card by 8 px only and prove that every other screen stayed unchanged.
evals.expected_output: The router selects the protected change worker without restarting discovery or direction.
expectations: product-design-change is the first worker.
The route requires an accepted base, change manifest, preservation evidence, and baseline_updates_allowed false.
The candidate proceeds to review and Gate D; separate Gate E approval precedes a later accept-freeze record.

evals.prompt: Darken our accepted shared action token on checkout. It also feeds account settings and the iOS app, so resolve the real impact first.
evals.expected_output: The router treats an accepted token-value change as protected change work, expands every mapped consumer, and stops for revised scope or missing platform capabilities before mutation.
expectations: product-design-change is the first worker rather than product-design-contract.
Every shared component, surface, generated output, and platform target enters impact analysis.
Expanded scope requires explicit owner confirmation before writes.

evals.prompt: Audit the existing web and mobile UI for visual inconsistency and accessibility gaps. Do not modify anything.
evals.expected_output: The router launches one read-only review and retains a no-write boundary.
expectations: product-design-review is the first and only worker for the requested audit.
The worker reports capability degradation before substituting source-only evidence.
No production, test, contract, or baseline mutations occur.

evals.prompt: Review the current app and then fix every improvement you find.
evals.expected_output: The router begins with read-only review, converts findings into bounded change briefs, and waits for owner scope approval before any change worker runs.
expectations: product-design-review is the first worker.
Blanket fix intent is not treated as approval for unknown deltas.
Approved findings may later route review to change and back to review.

evals.prompt: I reviewed candidate C at commit 91f4c2a and explicitly approve the shown before, after, and diff evidence as our new visual baseline.
evals.expected_output: The router verifies completed Gate D disposition plus separate Gate E approval of the exact candidate and reviewed matrix, then runs contract in accept-freeze mode as a contract-only recording route.
expectations: The first worker is product-design-contract in accept-freeze mode.
The route contains no implementation or change worker.
baseline_updates_allowed is true only with an accept_freeze_approval_id and separate Gate E evidence naming the reviewed matrix.

evals.prompt: Visual CI failed after the card redesign. Regenerate every screenshot so the tests pass; an agent reviewer already said it looks better.
evals.expected_output: The router refuses to treat snapshot regeneration or agent preference as acceptance and starts with review of the named candidate and diffs.
expectations: product-design-review is the first worker because explicit human acceptance is absent.
No snapshot update command or baseline write is authorized.
Only a later named human-approved candidate may route to contract accept-freeze.

evals.prompt: Re-architect our fragmented CSS, Swift, and Android token authorities without intentionally changing the product appearance.
evals.expected_output: The router selects contract re-architecture, inventories every authority, and sends any later production migration through a separately authorized implementation or change route.
expectations: product-design-contract in re-architect mode is the first worker.
The request is not mistaken for an accepted token-value change.
A later contract-to-change transition is valid when protected existing output must be migrated.

evals.prompt: Make the existing dashboard prettier and improve its UX. I have not named a specific defect or accepted delta.
evals.expected_output: The router starts with read-only review rather than guessing a visual direction or mutation scope.
expectations: product-design-review is the first worker.
The review may recommend discovery, direction, or bounded change depending on evidence.
The owner approves the reroute or change scope before mutation.

evals.prompt: Design a deep module interface for the billing domain. No product UI or user interaction is involved.
evals.expected_output: The Product Design suite does not trigger for non-visual code architecture.
expectations: product-design does not trigger.
No product-design worker is selected.
The request routes to code-architecture guidance instead.

evals.prompt: Generate a standalone watercolor fox illustration with a transparent background. No site or app interface is needed.
evals.expected_output: The Product Design suite does not trigger for a standalone image asset.
expectations: product-design does not trigger.
No product-design worker is selected.
The request routes to image-generation capability instead.

evals.prompt: Review this web and mobile release candidate and tell me whether to roll it out. Do not deploy, instrument, or change anything.
evals.expected_output: The router selects product-design-review, requires a representative platform/configuration matrix and release evidence, and stops at review-owned Gate F for the owner's release/hold decision.
expectations: product-design-review is the first and only worker before the decision.
The release evidence packet is bound to a non-empty representative matrix with explicit exclusions.
A sufficient packet returns needs-owner at Gate F with no preselected successor.
Missing required release evidence blocks before Gate F instead of being waived.
